newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies close weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies close weaker but off lows.

text.p: CME hog futures remained under pressure at the close from fund selling and commercial liquidation prompted by weak cash markets while pork bellies pared sharp losses and a limit decline on commercial support and mixed short covering, traders said.

Hog futures closed 1.675 to 0.025 cent per lb lower with December down 0.700 at 58.800 and February off most at 75.850 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.450 to 0.800 lower with February off 0.975 at 78.325 cents.
February hogs fell to a 2-1/2-week low earlier when sell stops added to pressure from weak cash markets, traders said.

"The futures market finally realized that the product market is in some trouble -- we've seen the pork cutout drop $4.50 since the first of December," said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst at Brock Associates Inc.
The weakness in cash pork prices is prompting packers to reduce slaughter operations, sources noted.
However, the reduced kill pace and ideas of light storings prompted late support in pork bellies which recovered from early carryover selling that hit sell stops, they said.
"We will continue to see kills come in well below a year ago for two reasons, the hogs just aren't there and packers are not making enough money to fight over them, Harper said.
USDA estimated hog slaughter for the week to date Tuesday at 691,000 head, below 704,000 in the same period last week and 710,000 last year.

Spillover pressure from hog futures sent belly prices tumbling after midsession with May briefly touching down the 3.000-cent limit before prices moved back up on commercial demand and local short covering. Cash belly prices were also the only product showing any strength at noon, they added.
Harper also sees pork belly storings remaining light in view of the lighter kills and this should support belly futures in relation to hog futures.
After the close, the CME reported last week's net in-movement at warehouses outside Chicago at 1.779 million lbs compared with earlier analysts' estimates of in 1.5 to 2.5 million lbs.

In hog options, LIT division of First Options bought February 78 and 79 calls. Smith Barney bought the June 74/68 put spread. Commission houses lightly sold June 76 calls and 74 puts, pit sources said.
